body.body:
Delivered in `master`, as two drafts and the structure that would hold the record.

**[DAF-000](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-000-federation-constitution.md)** — the constitution, independent of any platform. Point by point against what this function asked for:

- **What counts as delivered work** — a function declared in public before it was claimed, with an inspectable public result, that closes. Ongoing effort with no completion is not a function. Documentation, translation, review and operations count; the unit is the function, not the hour.
- **Who confirms it** — the assembly does, in the open, and any claim can be contested in the thread before the report is merged.
- **Weight** — one function is one point; completing a declared module awards one further point per function in it, because integration is the part that gets abandoned. The bar for what counts as one function rises over time.
- **Decay** — none. Points record history and are not deleted. Influence moves by dilution instead: a share falls only because other people deliver. That is also the only mechanism by which founding weight disperses.
- **Points to votes** — one point, one vote, non-transferable. Quorum is 30% participation of *active* points plus a simple majority of votes cast. Holders who neither voted nor delivered in the last three assemblies keep every point and leave the quorum denominator, so an abandoned unit cannot freeze the federation.
- **Resource requests against the last-resort rule** — a request is returned unjudged unless it states what was tried first and why no other route exists. Funding is granted one function at a time, each grant evaluated against the evidence of the last, so undelivered work degrades every proposal that references it.

**[DAF-001](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md)** — Phase 0, which is the answer to "nor the contract". Every earlier attempt at this targeted a chain and was abandoned before deployment, and the reason was never the design: a deployment demands funding, tokenomics and an audience before the federation has produced a single recorded decision. So the rules run first on a repository, where a public, ordered, tamper-evident log of who delivered what already exists for free. §6 states what that substrate does not give — no censorship resistance, no cryptographic guarantee, no anonymity, no custody — and §7 states the conditions under which it stops being enough.

The transferable instrument the earlier drafts describe is deliberately out (DAF-000 §6.1). It cannot exist on this substrate, and a transferable claim on pooled funds carries obligations the federation is not in a position to hold. The design is preserved and marked as not in force rather than deleted.

**[`federation/`](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/tree/master/federation)** now holds the record: unit records, assembly reports, resource requests, and a ledger reading zero of everything. Nothing is running in it — no unit, no points, no assembly. The next function is the first assembly, run against a delivery that already happened, to find out what these rules cost to operate before anyone else is asked to live under them.

Closing this one as delivered. What it did not settle is listed in [DAF-000 §9](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-000-federation-constitution.md#9-what-this-document-does-not-settle) — the substrate beyond Phase 0, the transferable instrument, the authority of councils, and how points convert into `uid` reputation. Those are separate functions, and the parameters above are starting values that no use has validated yet. Argue with any of them in a new issue.
